conceptZh: 短手大腳的橡膠恐龍助跑撲倒在亮滑地板上，用圓滾滾的肚子與大屁屁一路滑行撞翻一排彩色保齡球瓶與弧形積木，將它們精準撞疊成大大的「屁」字。
object: a chunky green rubber dinosaur toy with giant feet, tiny stubby arms, and a round bouncy bottom, plus a row of bright foam blocks and bowling pins
morph: A row of colorful bowling pins and curved foam blocks are knocked flying by the rubber dinosaur's belly slide, spinning and stacking mid-air into the outer 尸 canopy and the paired 比 legs of the character 屁 in solid deep cobalt blue.
creativeAngle: 結合「橡膠恐龍」手太短只能用全身衝撞的角色特質與「滑壘全倒（Belly Slide Pile-up）」的肢體喜劇模式：恐龍原本想用小短手推球瓶卻碰不到，乾脆助跑飛撲滑壘，撞擊瞬間還彈出俏皮小氣團，將弧形頂棚與成對的條狀積木撞成結構清晰的「屁」字，並在唸出「小屁屁」時拍拍自己搖晃的圓屁屁，讓語音、字義與搞笑動作完美同步。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animated slapstick clip in a bright, warm pastel-yellow playroom with a glossy wooden bowling lane floor, soft studio lighting, no pure white blowouts, and an uncluttered background.

0.0s–1.8s (Want It & Short-Arm Miss): On the left, a chunky lime-green rubber dinosaur toy with enormous feet, a big round bouncy bottom, and comically tiny stubby arms stares eagerly at a neat row of cobalt-blue foam blocks and bowling pins arranged center-right. It leans forward and wildly waves its tiny stubby arms trying to push the first pin, but its arms are way too short to reach, making it tip forward and wobble on its giant toes.

1.8s–3.5s (The Belly Slide Run-Up): As the warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin voice speaks the first syllable of "屁、屁、小屁屁" (ㄆㄧˋ、ㄆㄧˋ、ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄆㄧˋ ㄆㄧˋ), the rubber dinosaur puffs its cheeks, takes a big high-stepping run-up, and dives flat onto its round belly. A tiny harmless cartoon puff of air pops from behind its bouncy bottom, rocketing the dinosaur across the glossy floor like a speeding bowling ball straight toward the row of pins.

3.5s–5.0s (The Big Pile-Up Crash & Snap): BONK-CRASH! The sliding dinosaur plows straight through the row of cobalt-blue blocks and pins with joyful cartoon squash-and-stretch. As the voice clearly pronounces the second "屁" (ㄆㄧˋ), the flying pins and curved blocks spin and stack cleanly in the center of the frame into the exact Traditional Chinese character "屁" in solid, saturated deep cobalt blue: a curved top canopy with a long sweeping left-falling stroke (尸) sheltering the two side-by-side hooked leg shapes (比) underneath.

5.0s–8.0s (3-Second Hold & Payoff): The finished cobalt-blue glyph "屁" holds completely still, centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height against the light warm background for a full 3 seconds. Down in the lower-left margin completely clear of the strokes, the dizzy, grinning rubber dinosaur pops up onto its giant feet, turns sideways, and happily wiggles its round rubbery bottom in a proud strike pose right as the voice finishes saying "小屁屁" (ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄆㄧˋ ㄆㄧˋ).

Audio: Warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin voice reading slowly and distinctly with exact Taiwan standard tones: "屁、屁、小屁屁" (ㄆㄧˋ、ㄆㄧˋ、ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄆㄧˋ ㄆㄧˋ). Playful cartoon slide whistle, soft bowling-pin bonk, and a light bouncy pop; no extra speech, no subtitles or vocabulary text on screen, only the single centered character 屁.
